customManagers.description: The Artillery demo has no package.json, so Corepack is told the pnpm version on the command line and no built-in manager reads it.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Rewrite each demo's pnpm-lock.yaml every Friday so transitive dependencies pick up published fixes; ordinary updates and vulnerabilityAlerts only reach packages a package.json names. Renovate does not apply minimumReleaseAge here because pnpm regenerates the lockfiles, so pnpm enforces the same seven days through minimumReleaseAge in each pnpm-workspace.yaml, which is what makes automerge safe. Renovate still waits for every check on the branch.

packageRules.description: Merge eligible non-major updates after checks pass; keep unrelated dependencies separate.
Every packageManager field and every Corepack command has to name the same pnpm version, so they move in one pull request.
The WebdriverIO packages are released together and declare each other as peers, so updating part of the set breaks the browser demo.
The Jest demos differ only in the library each one shows, so their shared test tooling stays on one version.
Each Java demo carries its own wrapper and all of them have to run on the same Gradle.
A runtime major in .tool-versions also moves the Gradle toolchain, the README and the lockfiles, which Renovate does not touch, so a human finishes the update.
A major update can change what a demo shows on stage, so it waits for a review.
